hints: Focus on what sulfur dioxide can do in air, it is easily oxidised from S(+4) to S(+6) so it can act as a reducing agent.
Remember the key atmospheric reaction where $\text{NO}_2$ oxidises $\text{SO}_2$, this directly gives you the result for transformation 1.
Consider how $\text{SO}_2$ can be regenerated from $\text{SO}_3$ by oxidising $\text{NO}$ and $\text{CO}$, allowing it to act as a catalyst in a cycle.
walkthrough:
**Spot SO2 as a reducing agent**

Think like a teacher with your student. Sulfur in $\text{SO}_2$ is in oxidation state +4 and really wants to become +6 in $\text{SO}_3$ or sulfate. That means $\text{SO}_2$ can reduce another oxidising pollutant while itself being oxidised.

$$\text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 \text{ (S: +4 to +6, oxidation)}$$

**Check transformation 1: NO2 to NO**

Nitrogen dioxide is a good oxidiser. In the atmosphere it can oxidise $\text{SO}_2$ directly. Here $\text{SO}_2$ is the reagent, it is used up.

$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{NO}$$

**Check transformations 2 and 3: catalytic cycles**

Once $\text{SO}_3$ is formed, it is a strong oxidiser and can oxidise $\text{NO}$ back to $\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{CO}$ to $\text{CO}_2$. In both cases $\text{SO}_2$ is reformed, so it acts as a catalyst overall.

$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{NO} \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2$$
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{CO} \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{CO}_2$$

**Conclude all three are possible**

Statement 1 uses $\text{SO}_2$ as a reagent. Statements 2 and 3 use $\text{SO}_2$ / $\text{SO}_3$ as a catalyst cycle. So 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: This option includes only 1 and 2. It is incomplete because transformation 3 is also possible. $\text{SO}_3$ formed in the atmosphere can oxidise $\text{CO}$ to $\text{CO}_2$ while regenerating $\text{SO}_2$, so $\text{SO}_2$ catalyses CO oxidation.
options.B: This option includes only 2 and 3. It is incomplete because transformation 1 is also possible. The direct reaction $\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{NO}$ is a well known atmospheric reaction where $\text{SO}_2$ acts as a reagent.
options.C: This option includes only 1 and 3. It is incomplete because transformation 2 is also possible. $\text{SO}_3 + \text{NO} \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2$ regenerates $\text{SO}_2$, so $\text{SO}_2$ catalyses oxidation of NO to $\text{NO}_2$.
options.D: This option includes 1, 2 and 3 and is correct. In 1, $\text{SO}_2$ is a reagent reducing $\text{NO}_2$ to NO. In 2 and 3, the $\text{SO}_2$ / $\text{SO}_3$ pair acts as a catalyst to oxidise NO to $\text{NO}_2$ and CO to $\text{CO}_2$.
